claims.statement: ExecutionEngine.executeTask enforces a fixed preflight governance order: in-memory/durable duplicate and running-state guards, execution_recovery_hold and deep_agent_assurance_hold metadata checks (throwing EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED / DEEP_AGENT_ASSURANCE_HOLD), a pending execution-only approval check, a runtime-governance isAllowed check that cancels the task when the assigned agent is quarantined or circuit-breaker-tripped, then structural admission gates (loop-operator pause, assigned-agent availability, skill attribution, runtime@version admission returning RUNTIME_NOT_ADMITTED), and only afterwards CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask, PolicyDecisionService.evaluate, and GovernanceGateService tightening before queueing the task.

CommandRiskClassifier screens commands against ordered regex tiers (critical patterns and outside-workspace writes recommend deny; high and medium mutation patterns recommend require_approval; read-only patterns recommend allow) and is fail-closed: an unrecognized command defaults to MEDIUM risk with require_approval, never allow.

CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask elevates risk for sensitive keywords and local opencode execution, treats review_only tasks as low risk, defers to classify() when task.metadata.requested_command is present, and forces recommended_decision to deny whenever the resulting risk level is CRITICAL.

PolicyDecisionService.evaluate loads enabled approval_policies ordered by priority DESC then created_at DESC, applies the first matching policy, compiles policy match_pattern through ReDoSGuard (dangerous or invalid patterns never match), overrides to deny when the tool is in the policy's blocked_tools, and falls back to the classifier's recommended_decision when no policy matches.

GovernanceGateService is default-off (GOVERNANCE_GATE_ENABLED=true arms it), looks up OpenMythos benchmark evidence by task agent_id then nightly:<model> from GOVERNANCE_GATE_MODEL_MAP then metadata subject_model, returns allow when no evidence exists, and when the latest score is below the floor returns require_approval with a trend and optionally flagRetirement after three consecutive below-floor declining runs — it only ever tightens allow to require_approval and never loosens a deny or approval outcome.

GOVERNANCE_GATE_FLOOR defaults to 3, calibrated for a 0-5 score scale while observed openmythos_eval_runs.overall_score values range roughly 0-95, and floor() accepts any finite non-negative value (a former <=5 clamp was removed), so operators must set the floor explicitly when arming the gate or it only catches near-zero runs.

ToolBroker.evaluateToolCall rate-limits per principal (100 requests per 60s sliding window plus 10-per-second burst, throwing RateLimitExceeded), defaults to deny for unknown tools, escalates allow to require_approval at or above require_approval_above_risk (default HIGH), blocks self-allow after more than 5 allow decisions by the same principal on a task within one hour (separation of duties), and persists every decision with an immutable dec-<uuid> decision id in tool_broker_decisions.

ToolBroker capability tokens issued on allow are durable rows in tool_broker_capability_tokens scoped to category:tool, task, and principal with a 900-second default TTL; validateCapabilityToken requires tool, task, and presenting principal to all match and deletes expired tokens, and reevaluateOnParameterChange deletes the original token and re-runs the full evaluation when parameters change.

CLI executors do not mediate their internal tools through ToolBroker, so constructing a broker in ExecutionEngine does not enforce per-tool policy; callers must call evaluateToolCall before execution and validateCapabilityToken at the effect boundary themselves.

ApprovalService.createApproval stamps expires_at with approvalTtlMs() (APPROVAL_TTL_MS, default 1 hour, clamped to 5 min .. 7 days) and writes the approval row plus its required djimitflo.approval.requested outbox event (via enqueueRequiredEvent) and its canonical APPROVAL_REQUESTED audit entry in a single immediate transaction, so a failed audit or outbox insert rolls back the approval; the Telegram push, WebSocket broadcast, and best-effort authority-ledger recordDecision happen only after commit, and a broadcast failure is logged but never undoes the decision.

ApprovalService.decideApproval runs in an immediate transaction, rejects decisions on expired approvals (persisting expiry plus its audit and outbox event before throwing APPROVAL_EXPIRED, written exactly once), enforces self-approval prevention at the data layer by throwing SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN when decidedBy equals requested_by, and refuses to process a non-pending approval twice.

Approval expiry is realized lazily on read or on a decision attempt, and realize-expiry cancels a task still in awaiting_approval (guarded so tasks that moved on are untouched) with its own task_cancelled_after_approval_expiry audit row, mirroring what a denial does.

Manual-action approvals (metadata.manual_action: true, created via POST /api/approvals) never gate or resume execution: getLatestPendingForTask with executionOnly filters them via a json_type(metadata, '$.manual_action') != 'true' predicate before LIMIT so a newer manual review cannot hide an older execution gate, and handleApprovalDecision records their decisions as evidence and returns without dispatching.

Each approval lifecycle step produces two distinct side records: a post-commit best-effort authority_events ledger entry (sha-256 payload digest, per-correlation sequence, failures swallowed to null) via recordDecision, and a required djimitflo.approval.* event_outbox row enqueued by enqueueRequiredEvent inside the same transaction as the state change (rolling the approval back on insert failure, no-op while EVENT_PUBLISH_ENABLED is not true), later drained by EventOutboxService.publishPending (compare-and-set claims, retry cap of 10, stable dedupe_key djimitflo:<event_id>) to DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_URL.

ExecutionEngine.hasApprovedStart treats an approval as a valid execution grant only if it matches the executor kind, is not a manual action, has not expired, and its stored executionInputHash equals a fresh sha-256 hash of the task's dispatch-relevant fields — so any edit to title, description, tags, or instructive metadata, any executor-kind change, or expiry forces a new approval before dispatch.

executeTask revalidates admission after the runtimeConcurrencySemaphore capacity wait: the execution input hash must be unchanged and risk classification, policy evaluation, and gate assessment run again, with a tightened outcome aborting via EXECUTION_POLICY_DENIED or EXECUTION_APPROVAL_STALE rather than dispatching on stale authority; a granted approval resumes by re-entering executeTask.

AuditService is a façade over ComplianceAuditService: record() maps AuditEventCreateInput to appendEntry, deriving outcome from the event type (denied/violation to denied, failed/error to failure, else success) and defaulting actor to system, while both read and write the same audit_events table.

ComplianceAuditService.appendEntry hash-chains every audit_events row: previousHash is the latest entry's hash (or 'genesis'), hash is sha-256 over canonical JSON with deeply sorted keys, chain_sequence is MAX+1, SQLite triggers on audit_events and the compliance_audit_log view (including an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger preserving legacy writers) raise errors on UPDATE/DELETE making the log append-only, and verifyChain replays the chain checking linkage and recomputed hashes.

Admission is revalidated end-to-end after the runtimeConcurrencySemaphore capacity wait: the task must still be queued, its executionInputHash must be unchanged, and classification, policy evaluation, and gate assessment re-run; a tighter decision aborts with EXECUTION_POLICY_DENIED / EXECUTION_APPROVAL_STALE. fallbackAdmitted() applies the same classify-evaluate-approved-grant test to every fallback executor.

Approval grants are bound to the exact dispatch: ExecutionEngine.hasApprovedStart only honors an approved, unexpired, non-manual-action approval whose stored executionInputHash equals a fresh sha-256 over the task's dispatch-relevant bytes (runtime output and recovery stamps excluded) for the same executorKind; the opt-in LOOP_REVIEWER_APPROVAL_INHERIT=true escape lets read-only checker or security-checker tasks inherit their loop run's human-approved maker approval under strict conditions.

ToolBroker enforces pre-execution, per-tool-call policy with a default-deny fallback: evaluateToolCall rate-limits per principal (sliding 60-second window of 100 plus a 10-per-second burst throwing RateLimitExceeded), evaluates mcp_tool_call policies, escalates allow to require_approval at or above the HIGH risk threshold or on a maker-checker violation (more than 5 self-allows on one task per hour), and issues a durable cap-<uuid> capability token (default 15-minute TTL) persisted in tool_broker_capability_tokens, with every decision recorded in tool_broker_decisions.

ToolBroker does not mediate executor-internal tool calls: it performs no runtime syscall mediation, CLI executors do not route their internal tools through it, so callers must invoke evaluateToolCall() before execution and validateCapabilityToken() (which requires tool, task, and presenting-principal match plus unexpired token, deleting expired tokens) at the effect boundary; reevaluateOnParameterChange invalidates the original token and re-runs the full evaluation.

GovernanceGateService is default-off (armed by GOVERNANCE_GATE_ENABLED=true) and tighten-only: it consults up to 3 recent completed openmythos_eval_runs for the task's agent, then nightly:<model> from GOVERNANCE_GATE_MODEL_MAP, then subject_model metadata matches; no evidence means allow, a latest score below floor() yields require_approval with a trend, and three consecutive below-floor declining runs set flagRetirement as evidence only.

GOVERNANCE_GATE_FLOOR defaults to 3 and accepts any finite non-negative value without clamping: the earlier clamp to <=5 was removed because observed openmythos_eval_runs.overall_score values span roughly 0-95 in production, so the default catches only near-zero degenerate runs and the floor must be set explicitly when arming the gate.

manual_action approvals created via POST /api/approvals (metadata.manual_action: true) never gate execution: the engine's pending check and hasApprovedStart exclude them via COALESCE(json_type(metadata,'$.manual_action'),'null') != 'true' applied before latest-first ordering, and handleApprovalDecision records their decision as evidence without dispatching.

RuntimeGovernanceService.isAllowed(agentId) returns false only for quarantined or circuit-breaker-tripped agents, and ExecutionEngine's preflight check, plus the assertAssignedAgentAvailable re-check performed at every admission boundary (capacity wait, fallback attempt), cancels or refuses dispatch for blocked, retired, missing, or non-idle agents.

AuditService is the façade every pipeline stage calls: record() maps the rich AuditEventCreateInput onto ComplianceAuditService.appendEntry, deriving outcome from the event type (denied/violation to denied, failed/error to failure, else success) and defaulting the actor to system, while query() reads the same audit_events table.
